back: Government policies that aim to raise the productive capacity of the economy and shift long-run aggregate supply to the right.
Education and training, infrastructure, support for technology and research, tax incentives and deregulation.
Labour cost per worker ÷ output per worker.

front: Effect of a successful supply-side policy in AD/AS?
back: SRAS and LRAS shift right: higher real GDP and a lower price level.

front: Which supply-side policies work most slowly?
back: Education, training and infrastructure (years); tax incentives and deregulation act sooner.

front: Supply-side or demand-side: a cut in the interest rate?
back: Demand-side (monetary policy): it mainly shifts aggregate demand.

front: Name two costs or limits of supply-side policy.
back: Long time lags, high cost and uncertain results; it will not create jobs if demand is weak.
The maximum real output an economy can sustain with resources fully employed; shown by LRAS.
